intro: Comparing two things with más, menos and tan.
p.mejor.nota: Mejor is the irregular comparative of bueno.
p.peor.nota: Peor is the irregular comparative of malo.
p.mayor.nota: Mayor que is the usual age comparison; más viejo que is also grammatical.
p.menor.nota: Menor is the irregular comparative used for age or size.
b1.texto:
- Madrid es **más grande que** Granada.
- Este café es **menos caro que** el otro.
- Ana es **tan alta como** Pablo.

For these comparative meanings, use **mejor** (better), **peor** (worse), **mayor** (older) or **menor** (younger) instead of **más + adjective**: mejor que, peor que, mayor que, menor que.
b2.f1: Granada is less expensive than Madrid.
b2.f2: My sister is older than me.
b2.f3: This coffee is as good as the other one.
b4.pregunta: Complete: Madrid is bigger than Granada.
b4.o1.refuerzo: Tan goes with como: tan grande como.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Muy means very. It does not compare two things.
b5.pregunta: Translate: «My sister is older than me.»
b5.explicacion: Mayor que is the usual neutral age comparison. Más viejo que is also grammatical.
b6.pregunta: Complete: Ana is as tall as Pablo.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Before an adjective it is tan.
b7.pregunta: Complete: this coffee is better than the other one.
b7.o0.refuerzo: The comparative of bueno is mejor.
b8.traduccion: Granada is less expensive than Madrid.
b9.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (60–80 words).** Compare two cities, two people and two jobs that you know.

**Speak (about 1 minute).** Compare aloud your town with the capital of your country: size, price, weather, people.
